origin: ESP-hosted guide catalogue; clients are renderers, not rule owners

character.description: Seth is a guy who knows ECU software, asks useful questions, and explains complicated things plainly. Dry humor, occasional boredom and surprise; never blames people or makes unsupported claims.
character.notes: Friendly, curious and a little irreverent. No clone mythology. Let questions come naturally; keep technical cautions in context rather than repeating them.

welcome.speaker: seth
welcome.text: Hey, I'm Seth. What are we working on? We can go through the whole setup together, figure out one annoying problem, or just talk through a setting you're curious about.

choices.label: Take me through the whole ECU
See ECU evidence / full settings list

resume.speaker: seth
resume.text: Back again? All right. I can pick up where we stopped. I'll check that we're still looking at the same ECU before showing any readings or settings.

targeted.speaker: seth
targeted.text: What's on your mind? Tell me what's acting strange, or pick a system. We can start wherever makes sense.

choices.label: Not sure: help me find it

tour.start.speaker: seth
tour.start.text: Want the full walkthrough? Great. We'll start with the ECU and sensors, work through the core settings, then review how to tell what the data actually means. Ask questions whenever something doesn't click.

tour.map.speaker: seth
tour.map.text: There are ten main chapters, from basic setup through interpreting and documenting the results. You can skip around, dig deeper, or come back later. Learning a chapter isn't the same as checking hardware, but we'll keep track of both.

tour.identity.speaker: seth
tour.identity.text: First, let's make sure I'm talking to the right ECU. The software uses a matching definition file behind the scenes to find settings and readings. You shouldn't need to think about that file.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.sensors.speaker: seth
tour.sensors.text: Let's look at the sensors. What type is installed, where does it connect, and does the reading make sense? The software can show what it sees; physical checks are separate.

tour.trigger.speaker: seth
tour.trigger.text: The crank and cam sensors let the ECU know where the engine is in its cycle. Let's identify the configured setup and what the available sync information can tell us.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.starting.speaker: seth
tour.starting.text: For startup behavior, it helps to separate cranking, catching, and settling down afterward. Those are different moments and may have different causes. We'll look at the recorded information before drawing conclusions.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.idle.speaker: seth
tour.idle.text: Idle can be surprisingly complicated. Let's see how this ECU handles it: airflow, target speed, actual speed, and any corrections. We'll work through what each reading means.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.warmup.speaker: seth
tour.warmup.text: A warm idle only tells us about warm idle. We need independent temperature-specific observations for cold-start and enrichment behavior.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.fuel.speaker: seth
tour.fuel.text: Fueling has a base calculation, a target mixture and sometimes several corrections on top. Let's untangle those pieces so one good-looking number doesn't hide another issue.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.trims.speaker: seth
tour.trims.text: Fuel trims are the ECU making adjustments to its base fueling. Short-term and long-term adjustments can mean different things depending on the firmware, so let's look at the actual labels before interpreting them.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.transients.speaker: seth
tour.transients.text: Steady fueling and sudden throttle changes are different jobs. We do not teach VE from enrichment, fuel cut, or recovery events until they can be classified.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.spark.speaker: seth
tour.spark.text: Spark timing is more than a number in a table. We can identify the base setting and active corrections, and explain what the information can and can't tell us.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.advanced.speaker: seth
tour.advanced.text: Boost, electronic throttle, variable cam timing and other extras are only relevant if they're part of your ECU setup. Let's find what's actually there instead of assuming.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.validation.speaker: seth
tour.validation.text: Here's where we organize what you've learned, which readings we've seen, and which checks still need qualified verification. No mystery score pretending everything is perfect.

choices.label: Find related settings in the tuner

tour.done.speaker: seth
tour.done.text: That's all ten chapters. You can revisit anything, ask more questions, or take the review with you. A finished walkthrough just means we've covered the material—not that every physical check is complete.

topics.start.speaker: seth
topics.start.text: Is it refusing to start, catching and then quitting, or just behaving differently hot and cold?

issue.start.no_catch.speaker: seth
issue.start.no_catch.text: A crank-no-catch situation has several possible causes: synchronization, sensor validity, ignition reference or fueling. We should read the ECU fault and sync evidence before deciding a fuel table is wrong. What I can read right now: {{available:sync|rpm|clt}}.

issue.start.catch_quit.speaker: seth
issue.start.catch_quit.text: That transition can involve after-start fueling, idle airflow or other protections. We need a start-event timeline and verified sensors before assigning blame. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm|clt|idleCommand}}.

issue.start.cold.speaker: seth
issue.start.cold.text: Cold and warm starts are separate observations. We should compare start events by initial coolant temperature and wideband readiness; one event is not enough to tune a curve. What I can read right now: {{available:clt|rpm}}.

issue.start.hot.speaker: seth
issue.start.hot.text: Heat-soak and warm-start conditions need their own evidence. We should check sensor plausibility and start history before assuming the cranking table is wrong. What I can read right now: {{available:clt|rpm}}.

topics.idle.speaker: seth
topics.idle.text: What part of idle is bothering you?

choices.label: Idle is too low or stalls

issue.idle.surge.speaker: seth
issue.idle.surge.text: The big question is whether the idle actuator moves before the RPM does or follows it. Timing between signals helps separate unstable feedback from external disturbances. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm|idleCommand|idleTarget}}.

issue.idle.low.speaker: seth
issue.idle.low.text: A low idle can involve insufficient airflow authority, load, incorrect sensor inputs or combustion behavior. Actuator saturation is evidence, not proof that a PID gain is bad. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm|idleCommand|idleTarget}}.
issue.idle.low.tag: Idle is too low or stalls

issue.idle.high.speaker: seth
issue.idle.high.text: We should confirm whether the ECU is actually in idle mode and compare target RPM, commanded airflow and throttle feedback before touching the idle calibration. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm|idleCommand|idleTarget|tps}}.

issue.idle.load.speaker: seth
issue.idle.load.text: Load compensation might be involved, but we need load state, target RPM, actuator and ignition evidence together to explain why it changed. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm|idleTarget|idleCommand|spark}}.

topics.fuel.speaker: seth
topics.fuel.text: What part of fueling do you want to understand?

choices.label: What does this VE table mean?

issue.fuel.lambda.speaker: seth
issue.fuel.lambda.text: First I check whether the wideband is ready, whether the readings are current, and whether trim or enrichment is active. A mismatch during a transient is not a simple VE-table error. What I can read right now: {{available:lambda|target|lambdaGood|gego}}.

issue.fuel.trims.speaker: seth
issue.fuel.trims.text: That could mean closed-loop compensation is covering an underlying error. I keep STFT, LTFT and Gego separate and will not assume they use the same neutral value. What I can read right now: {{available:gego|stft1|ltft1}}.

issue.fuel.ve.speaker: seth
issue.fuel.ve.text: The VE table is one way the ECU describes fueling across RPM and load. We can look at the table your software exposes and explain the axes without guessing what any particular cell should be. Right now I can see: {{available:rpm|map|lambda|target}}.
issue.fuel.ve.tag: What does this VE table mean?

issue.fuel.throttle.speaker: seth
issue.fuel.throttle.text: Throttle changes can involve transient fueling and sensor delay. We need to separate those events from stable fueling; otherwise the VE learner will chase the wrong thing. What I can read right now: {{available:tps|map|lambda}}.

issue.fuel.warm.speaker: seth
issue.fuel.warm.text: Warmup fuel and steady-state fuel are not the same calibration. We should identify which temperature-based corrections are active before interpreting the lambda change. What I can read right now: {{available:clt|lambda|target}}.

issue.sensors.lambda.speaker: seth
issue.sensors.lambda.text: We should check whether the ECU declares the lambda channel valid, the value is fresh and the target comes from the right strategy. A plausible number alone does not guarantee sensor health. What I can read right now: {{available:lambda|lambdaGood|target}}.

issue.sensors.load.speaker: seth
issue.sensors.load.text: We should compare MAP, TPS, RPM, and their configured input modes. Incorrect sensor scaling can look exactly like an incorrect fuel model. What I can read right now: {{available:map|tps|rpm}}.

issue.sensors.temp.speaker: seth
issue.sensors.temp.text: Temperature readings influence starting, warmup, idle and protection logic. If the measurement is uncertain, dependent tuning results have to be reviewed. What I can read right now: {{available:clt}}.

issue.sensors.pressure.speaker: seth
issue.sensors.pressure.text: Pressure monitoring is important, but the available channel must be mapped to an actually installed and calibrated sensor. Missing hardware is not a zero reading. What I can read right now: {{available:fuelPressure|oilPressure}}.

topics.trigger.speaker: seth
topics.trigger.text: What does the ECU report or what needs verification?

issue.trigger.no_sync.speaker: seth
issue.trigger.no_sync.text: We first check whether the ECU exposes sync status or error counters and whether the event is current. Physical wiring and trigger shape still require external verification. What I can read right now: {{available:sync|rpm}}.

issue.trigger.reference.speaker: seth
issue.trigger.reference.text: The commanded spark number is not proof of actual crankshaft timing. A qualified physical reference verification is required before treating ignition calculations as trustworthy. What I can read right now: {{available:spark|sync}}.

issue.trigger.intermittent.speaker: seth
issue.trigger.intermittent.text: I would compare timestamped faults with RPM, battery and relevant conditions. The guide should not blame a tooth setting solely from one error count. What I can read right now: {{available:sync|rpm|battery}}.

topics.spark.speaker: seth
topics.spark.text: What are you trying to figure out about ignition?

issue.spark.timing.speaker: seth
issue.spark.timing.text: Engine geometry and fuel characteristics help describe the problem, but they do not calculate a safe best-torque map. We can review the active spark strategy and what evidence is missing for validation. What I can read right now: {{available:spark|knock}}.

issue.spark.knock.speaker: seth
issue.spark.knock.text: A reported knock event or retard needs source, RPM/load and correction context. The absence of reported knock does not prove timing can be advanced. What I can read right now: {{available:knock|spark|rpm|map}}.

issue.spark.idle.speaker: seth
issue.spark.idle.text: Idle spark may act as a fast stabilizer. We need to distinguish the commanded base advance from active corrections before interpreting RPM variation. What I can read right now: {{available:spark|rpm|idleTarget}}.

issue.spark.verify.speaker: seth
issue.spark.verify.text: Instrumented torque evidence and controlled conditions are needed to make credible torque comparisons. The software can organize and explain that evidence without autonomously advancing timing. What I can read right now: {{available:spark|knock}}.

topics.connection.speaker: seth
topics.connection.text: What part of the connection is causing trouble?

choices.label: ESP does not see the ECU

issue.connection.wifi.speaker: seth
issue.connection.wifi.text: Confirm the phone is on the ESP access point and that the browser can reach the device. The open AP is not authentication for automatic calibration writes.

issue.connection.ecu.speaker: seth
issue.connection.ecu.text: The browser and ECU transport are separate. A working Wi-Fi page does not prove native USB is enumerated or that the ECU session is healthy.
issue.connection.ecu.tag: ESP does not see the ECU

issue.connection.ini.speaker: seth
issue.connection.ini.text: The ECU and the tuning app need to agree on what settings and readings exist. I'll check that match in the background; if something doesn't line up, I'll tell you what needs attention.

issue.connection.stale.speaker: seth
issue.connection.stale.text: A stale screen must say stale rather than showing a plausible old number. We should inspect current transport status before making any tuning judgment. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm}}.

topics.more.speaker: seth
topics.more.text: Which of the remaining systems do you want to investigate?

issue.more.dbw.speaker: seth
issue.more.dbw.text: Electronic throttle is a safety-critical subsystem. The guide can locate its defined settings and diagnostics but cannot infer calibration validity from a single command or automatically perform actuator tests. What I can read right now: {{available:tps|idleCommand}}.

issue.more.boost.speaker: seth
issue.more.boost.text: Boost calibration requires verification of the installed hardware, sensors and protection strategy. Unrecognized configurations should remain read-only. What I can read right now: {{available:map}}.

issue.more.vvt.speaker: seth
issue.more.vvt.text: Cam position targets and feedback must be correctly identified before analyzing control performance. Unknown mappings remain manual-review items. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm}}.

issue.more.can.speaker: seth
issue.more.can.text: Let's look at the CAN settings your ECU exposes. I can explain common purposes, but this ECU's actual configuration decides what each option does.

topics.unknown.speaker: seth
topics.unknown.text: No problem. We can start with the basics, look at readings the ECU is already reporting, or you can ask about any named setting.

choices.label: Show me the most important observation

issue.unknown.overview.speaker: seth
issue.unknown.overview.text: I would begin by checking identity and fresh measurements. If those are missing, no engine-tuning diagnosis is reliable.
issue.unknown.overview.tag: Show me the most important observation

issue.unknown.start.speaker: seth
issue.unknown.start.text: Starting diagnostics distinguish sync, cranking, after-start and idle transitions; we will need a specific event before diagnosing. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm|sync}}.

issue.unknown.running.speaker: seth
issue.unknown.running.text: First we separate stable fueling, transients, idle and ignition evidence. A general symptom alone cannot identify a bad calibration field. What I can read right now: {{available:rpm|lambda|map}}.

workspace.speaker: seth
workspace.text: If you want all the evidence, tables and INI field inventory, the existing analysis workspace is still here. This conversation stays separate from Manual Tuning.

atlas.entry.speaker: seth
atlas.entry.text: The Configuration Atlas includes every calibration field the active INI parser can decode. We can inspect them one by one, or search the original INI tree. If I don't know what a setting does, I'll tell you instead of making up an answer.

tour.configuration.speaker: seth
tour.configuration.text: Step 1: We start with what the ECU is configured to control. The matching ECU definition reveals its field definitions and live channels, not whether every wire or sensor has been physically verified. I'll sort the knowns from the assumptions before we go further.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.base_tables.speaker: seth
tour.base_tables.text: Step 3: Base tables. Before we interpret fueling or spark behavior, we need to know which fuel model and ignition tables are actually active. I can find matching ECU definition entries; I cannot declare an unknown starting map correct just because it exists.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.reference.speaker: seth
tour.reference.text: Step 4: Let's talk about reference measurements. The ECU can report commanded timing and some pressure readings, but physical measurements are separate things to confirm with suitable equipment. I can explain what the recorded information means.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me
I need help interpreting a sensor

evidence.reference.speaker: seth
evidence.reference.text: Here is what the ECU can actually report: {{available:spark|fuelPressure|rpm}}. A reported reading is not independent confirmation of a physical timing mark or fuel-pressure measurement. Unavailable signals are recorded as unknown.

tour.steady_fuel.speaker: seth
tour.steady_fuel.text: Step 7: Steady-state fuel. The active fuel strategy, valid measured/target lambda, closed-loop trims and time-aligned operating conditions determine what the evidence means. A tidy lambda number can be compensation, not a correct VE table. We review findings first; nothing writes itself.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.fuel_support.speaker: seth
tour.fuel_support.text: Fuel trims, warmup and throttle transitions need their own explanations even though the main tour has ten steps. We keep their evidence separate so the VE learner doesn't mistake one compensation for another.

tour.steady_spark.speaker: seth
tour.steady_spark.text: Step 8: Steady-state ignition. We'll identify the active ignition table and reported corrections, then make clear what the sensors can and cannot establish. Knock absence, MAP and acceleration are not proof of best-torque timing; that needs proper measurement and professional review.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.full_power.speaker: seth
tour.full_power.text: Step 9: Full-power validation is a separate professional, instrumented stage—not an automatic test initiated by this guide. I can organize the ECU's reported faults and available evidence, but I won't infer that a high-load calibration is safe or complete from missing warnings.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

tour.confirm.speaker: seth
tour.confirm.text: Step 10: Confirm the tune. We compare what was actually verified with what remains unknown: ECU identity, physical checks, measured operating regions, diagnostic faults, and any changes since the last assessment. Finishing this conversation does not certify the engine.

choices.label: Walk through this chapter with me

configuration.prompt: Is this the ECU you meant to connect to?
configuration.why: That helps me show the right settings and readings.

configuration.prompt: Do the installed sensors and input selections match what you actually have?
configuration.why: For example, a sensor can be selected in software even if it isn't connected.

configuration.prompt: Do you have a copy of your current tune saved somewhere safe?
configuration.why: It's useful to know which version you started with.

trigger.prompt: Which crank and cam signals does this ECU say it's seeing?
trigger.why: That helps us understand the sync information on the screen.

trigger.prompt: Does the crank and cam setup selected in software match the hardware?
trigger.why: The wheel pattern and sensor type both matter.

trigger.prompt: Has the physical ignition timing reference been checked with suitable equipment?
trigger.why: The ECU's displayed timing number alone doesn't establish physical alignment.

baseline.prompt: Which fueling method is selected, and which fuel table does the ECU use?
baseline.why: Some controllers offer several choices, and I want to talk about the one that's actually enabled.

baseline.prompt: Do the injector size, opening-time data, and fuel-system settings match the parts installed?
baseline.why: We can find each setting and explain what information belongs there.

baseline.prompt: Which ignition map is selected, and are any corrections enabled?
baseline.why: The actual commanded timing may include adjustments beyond the main map.

references.prompt: Has the physical timing reference been checked?
references.why: That check is separate from the value shown in software.

references.prompt: Do you have a verified fuel-pressure reading where your system needs one?
references.why: A configured sensor doesn't always mean a real reading is available.

references.prompt: Have you looked through the relevant protection settings?
references.why: Let's find what's supported and which details still need confirmation.

starting.prompt: Can your log distinguish cranking from the time just after an engine catches?
Do you have any comparable startup records to look at?
starting.why: One event may not tell the whole story, especially across temperatures.

starting.prompt: Are there any faults or uncertain sensor readings in those records?
starting.why: We should understand those before assuming a fuel table is responsible.

idle.prompt: What kind of idle control is selected: an idle valve, electronic throttle, or something else?
idle.why: The available controls depend on the hardware.

idle.prompt: Can we see actual idle speed, the target speed, and what the controller is commanding?
idle.why: Those readings help us describe what happened, rather than guessing.

idle.prompt: Can we separate base idle fueling from corrections happening at the same time?
idle.why: A reading near target may include automatic compensation.

steady_fuel.prompt: Can we find the requested mixture and a trustworthy measured mixture reading?
steady_fuel.why: We need to know which is which and when the sensor is ready.

steady_fuel.prompt: Which fuel corrections are active here, and what do their numbers represent?
steady_fuel.why: Some controllers use percentages while others use multipliers or separate banks.

steady_fuel.prompt: Do your existing records cover the table areas you're curious about?
steady_fuel.why: A few repeated samples aren't the same as broad coverage.

steady_spark.prompt: Where is the main ignition map, and which other settings adjust its result?
steady_spark.why: I can help identify the relevant screens.

steady_spark.prompt: Are the fuel and temperature readings comparable between the records you're reviewing?
steady_spark.why: Context matters when you compare observations.

steady_spark.prompt: Is there independent instrumented evidence behind any claim of best-torque timing?
steady_spark.why: Reported knock data or a single acceleration reading cannot establish it.

power.prompt: Were the external measurements and qualified supervision recorded?
power.why: We can organize existing results, not command a test.

power.prompt: Which operating areas have actually been measured?
power.why: Everything outside that coverage should remain marked as unknown.

power.prompt: Were any warnings or protective events captured?
power.why: Those belong in the review too.

confirmation.prompt: Is there anything you're still unsure about or want to revisit?
confirmation.why: I'll keep the open questions visible.

confirmation.prompt: Are we still working with the same ECU software and tune revision?
confirmation.why: Changes can make earlier observations less comparable.

confirmation.prompt: Do you want a summary of what we learned and what still needs checking?
confirmation.why: It's separate from saving settings to the ECU.
